title: Totally acyclic modules are acyclic for every ringed-topos direct image
statement: Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be sites small in a common coefficient universe [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], with sheaves of commutative rings $\mathcal O_{\mathcal C},\mathcal O_{\mathcal D}$. Let $f:(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C),\mathcal O_{\mathcal C})\to(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D),\mathcal O_{\mathcal D})$ be a morphism of ringed topoi [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism], with its induced module direct image [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For a sheaf of sets $K$ on a site $\mathcal T$ and an $\mathcal O_{\mathcal T}$-module $N$, put $\Gamma(K,N)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal T)}(K,N_{\mathrm{sets}})$ with pointwise abelian-group operations, and put $H^q(K,N)=R^q\Gamma(K,-)(N)$, computed by injective resolutions in the module category [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Let $N$ be an $\mathcal O_{\mathcal C}$-module that is totally acyclic, meaning $H^q(K,N)=0$ for every sheaf of sets $K$ on $\mathcal C$ and every $q>0$. Then $$R^qf_*N=0\quad(q>0)$$ in $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_{\mathcal D})$, where the right derived functors of module direct image are computed by injective resolutions. No flatness of the structural ring map is assumed, and the geometric morphism need not come from a functor between the given sites.

source.place: Tag 0731 (lemma-limp-acyclic), assertion (4); Tag 072Y (definition-limp) and section-limp for total acyclicity.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck] and [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives], the module category on $\mathcal C$ has enough injectives. Choose a nonnegative injective resolution $N\to I^\bullet$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions]: embed $N$ into $I^0$, embed its cokernel into $I^1$, and repeat with successive cokernels. Put $J^\bullet=f_*I^\bullet$. By the meaning of the right derived functors in the statement, $R^qf_*N=\mathcal H^q(J^\bullet)$.

source.place: Tag 0731 (lemma-limp-acyclic), assertion (4), and Tag 072W (lemma-higher-direct-images), injective-resolution argument; section-limp, definition of H^q(K,N). Direct adjunction version written by Q67.

proof.text: For $V\in\mathcal D$, let $h_V=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal D}(-,V)$ and $K_V=f^{-1}(h_V^\#)$. Sheafification adjunction [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], evaluation at $\mathrm{id}_V$ [lem-galois-yoneda-hom-bijection], and the topos adjunction [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism] give, for every source module $M$, $$ (f_*M)(V)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(h_V^\#,f_*M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(K_V,M)=\Gamma(K_V,M). $$ These are isomorphisms of abelian groups: evaluation and sheafification adjunction preserve pointwise operations; transposing $a x+y$ gives $f^\sharp(f^{-1}a)\widetilde x+\widetilde y$, so setting $a=1$ proves additivity of the last bijection. All maps are natural in $M$, hence commute with each differential of $I^\bullet$. Consequently $J^\bullet(V)\cong\Gamma(K_V,I^\bullet)$ as complexes of abelian groups.

source.place: Tag 0731 (lemma-limp-acyclic), assertion (4), and Tag 072W (lemma-higher-direct-images), injective-resolution argument; section-limp, definition of H^q(K,N). Direct adjunction version written by Q67.

proof.text: Fix $q>0$. The same module injective resolution computes $H^q(K_V,N)$ by the definition in the statement. Total acyclicity therefore gives $$H^q(J^\bullet(V))\cong H^q(\Gamma(K_V,I^\bullet))=H^q(K_V,N)=0$$ for every $V$. In particular, every section $z\in J^q(V)$ with $d^qz=0$ equals $d^{q-1}y$ for some $y\in J^{q-1}(V)$. This uses the actual sheaf of sets $K_V$, without requiring that it be represented by an object of $\mathcal C$.

source.place: Tag 0731 (lemma-limp-acyclic), assertion (4), and Tag 072W (lemma-higher-direct-images), injective-resolution argument; section-limp, definition of H^q(K,N). Direct adjunction version written by Q67.

proof.text: Kernels in the module-sheaf category are sectionwise [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Thus $Z^q=\ker(d^q:J^q\to J^{q+1})$ has sections the cycles just considered. Step 3 says that $J^{q-1}\to Z^q$ is surjective on every set of sections, so its sectionwise cokernel presheaf is zero. Its cokernel as a module sheaf is the sheafification of that presheaf, again by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and is zero. This cokernel is $\mathcal H^q(J^\bullet)=R^qf_*N$, as required.
